_description: Battle simulator v1 (tools/nn/sim, docs/en/training/simulator.md): the numbers that are neither in a unit passport (config/nn/units.json) nor in the game's rules (config/nn/game_rules.json). Each is measured in the game or calibrated to a measurement (docs/en/training/measurements.md); `why` says which. Written by hand; python -m tools.nn.sim.check compares the simulator with the game.

step_s.why: morale rises 2 points a second before contact in every recording (+0.057 MoralePercent/s at leadership 35 ... +0.029 at 70) = one point (minimium_increment_update_per_tick) per 0.5 s tick

battle_limit_s.why: network plan: 60 minutes, the attacker loses on time

map_half_m.why: measured: routing units leave the map at |x| or |z| = 1020 m (Crossroads flat, 28 runs)

formation.why: spacing_m: a man's place across the front and between ranks for a unit WITHOUT a formation template (every unit of ours has one: config/nn/units.json spacing, the database's unit_spacings close formation of land_units.spacing - Empire infantry and lords 1.48 x 1.6 m, clanrats / clanrat spearmen / flagellants / militia 1.6 x 1.7, greatswords 1.7 x 1.75, stormvermin 1.8 x 1.9, skavenslaves 1.6 x 1.8, slingers / night runners 2.2 x 2.8, archers 2.0 x 2.1). files = floor(ordered width / h), front files x h, depth ceil(men / files) x v: the game's own formations (data/roster, 6 units, 15-80 m) give front (files - 1) h within 1.3 % (median), depth (ranks - 1) v within 14 % (wide fronts deeper: scatter); build/meleecore/spacing_check.py. Before 06.10.2026: 1.5 m for every unit (an arena spearmen fit). build/mass/spec.md read the template's numbers one row off (1.65 x 1.75 for the Empire: the next row's): the table's rows put nine floats BEFORE the key; that layout reads all 164 rows to the last byte (tools/nn/dbtables.py unit_spacings) and fits the roster depths (1.65 x 1.75 gave the Empire's depth x0.77-0.92).

turn.why: formation_deg_s / single_deg_s: out of melee a standing unit (not walking) turns in place at most this fast (a lord or another single entity: single_deg_s); a walking unit faces the way it walks, in melee contact.melee_turn_deg_s holds. Measured 04.10.2026 (build/p3, all 210 arena runs with 1 s samples since 30.09): missile units standing out of melee whose engine target becomes an enemy 60 deg or more off their bearing faced it within 20 deg after 1 s (median; mean 1.6 s for 60-120 deg, 1.7 s for 120-180 deg; 97 % of 160 within 15 s), (angle - 20) / seconds p25 45 / p50 64 / p75 117 deg/s - a lower bound, a turn done within the second counts a whole second; turning episodes of standing units (mv off, < 0.3 m/s, out of melee, >= 60 deg): missile infantry p50 81 deg/s (858), melee infantry 72 (23: they rarely stand and turn), lords 40 (p25 31, p75 66; 440 episodes, 2 s for 60-100 deg). 80 for formations, 40 for single entities. Before: the bearing was set at once, so a standing shooter facing away shot at once.

contact.pursuit_why: pursuit_rate: a routing enemy is struck with every man the contact holds (no ramp) at this share of the rule, from the rear (as before), without the striker's charge (absent: off). Before, a unit touching only routing enemies struck nothing: its contact clock counts standing enemies only, so its ramp stayed 0 (a lone spear, sword or clanrat unit ordered to attack a router for 30 s, touching it all 60 steps, dealt 0 HP; build/prespec/probe_sim.py). Measured (build/prespec/specs.md item 3, build/prespec/pursuit.py, 171 battles): a target one non-missile pursuer within 12 m of its centre aims at, with none of its own units near and nobody shooting it, loses 18.1 HP/s routing (6,090 s) against 28.4 standing in melee (54,292 s): 0.64 (95 % CI 0.56-0.75); within 20 m 0.52 (0.45-0.60); every unit type about half. No charge burst: the first 5 s of a pursuit 17.9 against 18.2 HP/s later (a standing target: 33.0 against 26.6, the charge). Fitted with the same measure on the simulator's gate battles (network against ai_like, build/prespec/pursuit_cal.py): pursuit_rate 0 / 0.5 / 1.0 gives 0.15 / 0.49 / 0.97 of the standing rate, linear between, so 0.65 gave 0.64 (about 170 pursuit seconds in 16 battles: +-0.1) with the old rout_speed 0.86. Refitted with rout_speed 0.985 and the rest of batch 2 (build/batch2/run.py gap: the gate's battles, 8 copies, the same measure): 0.65 -> 0.90 (29.9 HP/s routing, 273 s; standing 33.2), 0.35 -> 0.55 (18.3 HP/s, 294 s; standing 33.5), linear between: 0.43 gives 0.64 (routers now flee nearly as fast as their pursuers run, so the seconds within 12 m are more often the first of a rout). Relative to the simulator's own melee, which is stronger than the game's (33-35 against 28.4 HP/s standing); in absolute HP/s 0.35 already gives the game's 18.1.
contact.pin_why: pin_s / pin_melee_s: a unit leaving melee (leave_m) stays held this long in contact (not striking, struck), then walks out: a missile unit pin_s, a unit without a missile weapon pin_melee_s; a lone man (a lord) is not held (the game's lords break off melee 1.3 times a minute, out of melee after 3 s, median). leave_taken: the HP a leaving unit still in contact takes (held or walking) x melee (a unit without a missile weapon) / x missile (a missile unit). Melee units, measured (build/prespec/specs.md item 2, build/prespec/leave.py, 163 network battles with companion logs, 855 episodes of a unit in melee given a withdraw or a move 10 m or more away): still in melee 0.98 / 0.94 / 0.91 / 0.84 / 0.84 / 0.59 / 0.51 / 0.21 at 2 / 4 / 5 / 8 / 10 / 15 / 20 / 24 s (Kaplan-Meier), out after 21 s (median, battle bootstrap 11-24; the database's melee_breakoff_secs 24); it stands meanwhile (moved 0 m, median); it kills x0.00 of the attack rate from its 2nd second (x0.15 in the 1st); it takes x1.23 (0.99-1.53) of the HP share a unit of its class attacking takes, missile units x0.62 (0.40-0.89). The simulator walked melee units out in 3-4 s (none in melee at 4 s) and they took x0.62, missile units x1.13. The older count (8 battles of one gate, 0.81 in melee 3 s later) said melee units are not held. Missile units (pin_s): measured 04.10.2026 (sim task 2, build/p2/miss.py): the network's missile units in melee given a move or withdraw to a point 15 m or more away, all 93 network runs with companion logs from 02.10.2026 (254 episodes): share still in melee (Kaplan-Meier, an order change censors) 0.95 / 0.82 / 0.57 / 0.34 / 0.25 at 2 / 4 / 6 / 8 / 10 s, out after 6-7 s (median), escape 0.065-0.077 a second, still in melee 3 s later 0.85 (gate 20261004-071805: 0.93); the simulator (both sides replayed on that gate's 8 battles) walked them out in about 2 s (0.53 at 2 s, 0.24 a second, 3 s later 0.38). At 5 s: 0.076 a second, out after 6 s, 3 s later 0.88. Superseded (8 battles of one gate): melee units stayed as in the game without a hold (their enemies followed them: 0.83 / 0.76 at 4 / 5 s against the game's 0.83 / 0.80, 0.048 against 0.041 a second); held too, 0.94 were still in melee 3 s later (game 0.81).
contact.why: reach, lord_max_attackers, lord_splash_struck, lord_gather_s, reset_s: core_why. lord_max_attackers / lord_direction / lord_rival_others / lord_incidental: the lord swarm probe (01.10.2026, docs/en/game/units/lord-swarm.md; 3 battles, a lord standing, attacked by 1-4 infantry units from front, back and flanks, 5 repeats a layout, lords held by script so no abilities): the lord loses the same whatever the number of units (General 7.8 / 8.3 / 8.7 / 7.4 HP/s with 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 clanrat units, Warlord 6.2 / 5.8 / 5.1 / 4.8 with Empire spearmen); 4-5 enemy soldiers stand within 2.5 m of him, 7-10 within 3 m, shared by the units; an armour-piercing unit counts by its share (General: halberds alone 21.5, with one spear unit 16.1, with three 10.7). So the men striking a lord are capped in all (lord_max_attackers, core_why) and summed, split between the units by their contact; from his back or flank they hit him as from the front (lord_direction 0: the share of the database's flank/rear rule against a lone man). lord_rival_others: with the enemy lord on him too, the infantry's rate counts at this share (whole battles, a lord in melee not shot at: the enemy lord alone 14.5 HP/s, with 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 units targeting him too 18.6 / 10.6 / 15.1 / 20.4; the probe's lord-and-units trials, noisy: 0.7 +- 0.5). lord_incidental: a unit whose attack order is on another enemy strikes a lord it only touches at this share (whole battles: one enemy unit in contact, its current target another: 1.7 HP/s; him: 4.1). Front = within 60 deg of the facing (shield_defence_angle_melee 60), rear = beyond 120 deg. melee_turn_deg_s: a formation in melee turns no faster (a lord at once): measured in the 28 whole battles, infantry in melee standing turns 1 deg/s (median, mean 2.3; 20.8k seconds), a free unit struck in the flank turns 8 deg in the next 5 s (median, 653 contacts). step_m: a unit whose point is nearer does not turn to walk there (formations step back or aside facing the enemy); without it, units replayed to their recorded points stood with their backs to the enemy at contact in the pairs; leave_m: any unit in melee told to move this far or farther leaves the fight like a withdraw (0: off): it strikes nobody and is not held in place, the enemies in contact still strike it. Melee units (03.10.2026, build/gap/leave.py, melee_orders.py; the sim-to-game gap of the gate build/nn-gate/20261003-030449): our non-missile non-lord units in melee by the order in force, all 99 fair network runs with companion logs: attack 0.186 kills/s and 0.0026 HP share lost/s (129.8k unit-s), hold 0.225 / 0.0038, move to a point 10 m or more away 0.012 / 0.0045 (3.9k unit-s, moving 99 % of the time), withdraw 0.004 / 0.0038; in the gate itself attack 0.415 / 0.0035, move 0.007 / 0.0050 (34 % of our melee unit-seconds). So a melee unit moving away deals ~6 % of its attack rate and takes ~1.7x the damage; it stays in contact 97.5 % of the next seconds. The simulator kept it fighting at full rate (a move in melee was a free no-op, which the network learned to use: 45 % of its non-missile melee seconds in that gate against 0-2 % in earlier gates). The replay (tools/nn/sim/replay.py) moves such a unit to its recorded point only where that point is a move order in force: the network's units and missile units; CA's planner's and the game's AI's melee units with a far recorded point fight on in the game (the planner's: 0.17-0.29 kills/s in every direction, its point often the enemy's start beyond the enemy; build/simbatch/leave_dir.py), and leaving them made the spearmen-clanrats pair wrong. With it: the check's same winner, the network's battles 44 -> 47 of 93 (the 8 gate battles of build/nn-gate/20261003-030449: 4 -> 7 of 8; at 4 replays 4 + 1 split -> 7), the game-AI battles 22 of 26 both, mechanics 50 -> 51 of 54. Missile units, measured 02.10.2026 (build/simacc/missile_break.py, 28 game-AI and 63 network battles): the game's missile units in melee without a target and with their order point 10 m or more away were moving 45-78 % of those seconds and left melee after 10-12 s (median), against 19-36 s and 2-18 % moving for those holding near their point; the simulator keeps missile units in melee 284 s a battle against the game's 162 (median spell 15 s against 8). At 10 m (and the replay moving such units instead of fighting the nearest enemy) the check got no better (same winner 19 of 26 and 37 of 63 with the two lord numbers below; 20 / 36 without it), so it stays off. Task 20 (02.10.2026): on at 10 m together with lord_v_lord 0.73, lord_fall 0 and the database set (sim.json morale why): each alone lowered the winners because the errors compensated each other; together with the rest the winners hold (game-AI 18 of 26, network 43 of 71 against 20 / 43 with all off) and more battles end as in the game. lord_v_lord / lord_hit_slope: removed (core_why). unit_incidental: a unit attacking another enemy strikes an incidental enemy unit at this share. Use 1.0 after contact-phase replay synchronisation (build/gap5/replay_task; 4 copies, seed 1, 2 m jitter, both sides replayed). Gates 20261004-230630 / 20261004-071805 / 20261003-204730: game trade -0.306 / -0.260 / -0.407; at game end, phases with 0.3: -0.036 / +0.054 / -0.156, 0.6: -0.057 / -0.034 / -0.209, 1.0: -0.090 / -0.080 / -0.252; at sim end, 1.0: -0.152 / -0.086 / -0.280. Mean absolute trade error at game/sim end: 0.3 0.278/0.269, 0.6 0.225/0.202, 1.0 0.184/0.151. Matched check (CUDA battles, CPU mechanics, original 132 decided network battles, 8 copies): old replay 22/26 AI and 81/132 network; phases 0.3 22/26 and 78/132, 0.6 22/26 and 91/132, 1.0 23/26 and 98/132; mechanics 51/54 throughout. The old 0.3 fit used clock-indexed replays (game 19.6 HP/s, sim 33.9 at 1 and 22.3 at 0.3) and may have compensated for their contact errors. Contact starts/melee-second now 0.0300 (game 0.0300), but running entries 85.1% against 97.8%: fidelity is still incomplete. hold_rate: a unit without a missile weapon under HOLD in melee (no attack order) strikes at this share of its rate (calibrated, 04.10.2026, sim-to-game gap 3, P4; build/gap3/p4/kills.py, holdatk2.py, kills_cmp.py). The game, all fair network runs with companion logs (the network's own orders), our melee units in melee, not moving, health >= 0.3, matched on own and nearest enemy unit keys: under HOLD they kill 0.80 of what the same units kill attacking (the game's own kill count, 14.8k matched unit-s) and an enemy unit fighting them alone loses 0.66-0.74 of the HP; held units with an engine target (18 % of held melee seconds) fight like attacking ones, without one 0.56-0.70: the game fights only a held unit's men in contact. Missile units 0.99-1.01: not for them. The simulator gives a held unit its full rate on every side in contact (an attacking one only 0.3 on enemies other than its target), so with the measured 0.75 the held units of the gate battles (20261004-071805 + seed 1000900014, 2.3 enemy units in melee within 40 m, as in the game) still killed 0.26 a second in the replay and 0.27 against ai_like against the game's 0.17; at 0.5: 0.18 / 0.18 (attacking units: game 0.24, against ai_like 0.23). Before (full rate) the network learned to hold in melee: n3 held 76 % of its melee seconds in the simulator, killing 0.33 a second there; n3 against ai_like on those 8 battles +0.19 (game -0.27), at 0.75 +0.07, at 0.5 -0.08 (same winner 2 / 4 / 7 of 8); both sides replayed -0.100 / -0.065 / -0.089 (same winner 6 / 5 / 7).
contact.core_why: The melee core (06.10.2026). reach_m / lord_reach_m: formations touch when their edges overlap by -reach_m: in the game they step 2.5-4.8 m into each other at first contact - centre distance at first contact in the pairs spearmen v slaves 10.7 / 11.6 / 12.8 m, spearmen v clanrat spearmen 7.5 / 8.6 / 12.5 m (build/mass pair_contact.py) against half the sum of their depths with the database's spacing, 13.8 / 12.45 m at 30 m fronts: -2.1 / -2.9, so -2.5 (was 1.0 with 1.5 m spacing for everyone, when the depths matched by chance; the pairs' HP/s hardly move between -3.5 and -2). A lone man (a lord) stops at a formation's edge, lord_reach_m 1.0 (the old reach; build/mass/spec.md M5: his centre ~1.7 m before the edge): at -2.5 the lords barely touched their infantry in the pairs (steady 0.35-2.9 HP/s against the game's 5.5-8.2). lord_max_attackers: refitted with the database hit chance: 6.5 (General v clanrat spearmen, his steady loss -6 %, Warlord v spearmen +24 %; 5.5: -20 / +5 %; was 9 at hit_slope 0.1). lord_splash_struck: a lord's splash blow on a formation strikes this many men on average, each taking 1 / splash_max_attacks (4) of it: measured 2.07 (506 blows of the lord-in-a-crowd probe, 1.84-2.30 over 13 layouts, build/damage/spec.md D6; the old rule struck min(4, men), which with the database hit chance doubled a lord's damage on infantry). The pairs: General v clanrat spearmen +13 %, Warlord v spearmen +31 % (their fights end 22-26 % early) - the probe's crowd (1-4 units round him) may strike more men than one unit in front; left as measured. lord_gather_s: men round a lone man gather over this long from the striker's contact (linear from 0; the rate of a formation striking him): the pairs' first 15 s - a lord loses 38 / 45 HP in the game, 130 / 119 without it, 48 / 46 at 20 s - the old ramp_s kept only here (the lord swarm probe: 4-5 men within 2.5 m of him). reset_s: the melee clock (contact_s) restarts only after this long out of contact (the game: pull-outs of 4-7 s give 0.96x of the steady rate, no fresh fight, build/cyclecharge; before 0.5 s out restarted it). REMOVED: lord_v_lord (off since 06.10.2026) and lord_hit_slope 1 (lord against lord at the database rule): every blow uses the database hit chance now; the lone duels' numbers: docs/en/game/mechanics/melee.md.

melee.why: Melee by the game's rules (the melee core, 06.10.2026; docs/en/game/mechanics/melee.md, docs/en/training/simulator.md). Hit chance: the database rule 35 + attack - defence within 8-90 % at weight 1 (melee_hit_chance_*, melee_hit_chance_normalisation_coefficient 1; CA Feature Focus #2: Damage) for every blow. REMOVED with it (fitted, replaced by the rules): hit_slope 0.1 (formations: 'the pairs show the same losses whatever attack - defence is'; the 121 recorded formation battles fit slope 1 once a miss costs time, build/hitchance); flank_slope 2.0 / rear_slope 0.25 (the defence lost from the flank / rear counted at those weights; now the database's x0.6 / x0.3 at weight 1: a lone flank attacker in the game takes 1.53x, from the rear 1.92x, build/conform/master.md M4-M5); impact 1.5 (a charging formation's damage x2.5 over 13 s: no such rule, a charge is its bonus only - CA; the game's damage after contact is 1.31x the 10-20 s rate for a charge bonus <= 6 and 2.24x for >= 8, the simulator gave 5.6-8.3x, build/charge/spec.md 2.1); ramp_s 20 (a unit that did not charge brought its men to bear over 20 s: in the game a charged unit answers in full from the first second, 1.06x, build/charge/spec.md 2.2; kept only for men round a lone man: contact.lord_gather_s). miss_s: blows a second a fighting man = p / (p x attack interval + miss_s): the interval runs after a hit, a miss costs about 0.5 s (fitted on 121 recorded battles, 52 formation pairs, 20,034 s: build/hitchance fit2 / fit3); a lone man striking a lone man (lord against lord) swings every interval, p / interval (the lone lord duels: 0.103 blows a second, 41 % of the blows every 4 s hit, database 40 %). fighting_files: men striking = this share of the striker's files in contact (the contact's length over its own spacing across the front, or between ranks on a flank: config/nn/units.json spacing, the database's formation template); refitted with the rest on the four pairs' steady HP/s (tools/nn/sim/check.py; build/meleecore/sweep.py): 0.5 / 0.55 / 0.6 give spearmen v clanrat spearmen own -20 / -13 / -5 %, enemy +7 / +18 / +28 %, spearmen v slaves own -14 / -6 / +1 %, enemy +13 / +25 / +36 %: 0.5 (10 of the spearmen's 20 files; was 0.75 at hit_slope 0.1 and 1.5 m). The game's first 15 s of contact are stronger than the rule gives (the pairs' targets lose 499-764 HP, the simulator 396-446 without impact): not explained by the charge rule (spearmen's charge bonus is 4) - left to the in-game charge probe (build/charge/spec.md 7). splash_divides: a splash blow's damage is divided among the men it strikes, 1 / splash_max_attacks each (CA 5.1.0; measured: single blows of 47-57 HP on stormvermin), then armour and overkill; how many it strikes: contact.lord_splash_struck. braced_speed: a unit with charge_reflection slower than this (m/s) is braced: it strikes a charger within bracing_attack_angle 80 deg of its front at charge_reflect_damage_multiplier x2 while the charger's charge is at least charge_reflect_min_charge_factor_threshold 0.7 (the first 3.9 s; the database, CA: 'within 3.9 seconds of their charge, the Spearmen will do double damage'); it gets no charge of its own (before: a braced unit met a frontal infantry charge as a charge, fitted to braced spearmen charged head-on losing 0.80 of what the charger loses, 87 contacts).

charge.why: The charge by CA's rule (build/charge/spec.md; CA Feature Focus #2): an attack order and a run-up give the full charge bonus at contact - + bonus to melee attack (weight 1, like all attack) and + bonus to weapon damage split by its armour-piercing share - falling linearly to 0 over charge_decay_duration 13 s from the first blow, on its own clock: leaving contact neither stops nor restarts it, a new charge does (state `charge`). min_speed_share: run-up counts only at this share of the run speed or faster (the Empire's walk is 0.5 of its run, Skaven 0.36: not a charge; a run is; ours - the game asks for the charge speed). min_runup_m: metres of such run-up since the last stop, walk or contact (the game: 'a minimal run, only to play the animation'; the game's lords re-entering melee after < 20 m or at a walk show no burst, 1.0x, after >= 20 m at a run 1.25x, build/cyclecharge): pulling out and walking back in gives no fresh charge (the simulator gave 2.1-2.6x for that cycle, the game 1.0x). order_grace_s: an attack order given this long after the contact still charges if the run-up was there (the network runs in with a move and attacks at once; such contacts hit as charges in the game, build/prespec/specs.md item 6). Before (removed): any order at >= 0.5 of the run speed charged, the charge's size = speed / run, it ended when the unit left contact and 0.5 s out restarted it; a braced unit charged back. rush_m: a unit running at its attack target closes the last rush_m at its charge speed (the database's charge_speed, 14-27 % above the run): OFF (0) - whole battles show no rush in the last 7 s before contact (0.90-0.98 of the run, 3,729 approaches of the game's AI and 2,801 of ours, build/mass/spec.md S4); a switch for the in-game check. Not modelled (why): the charge's morale +15 (the recordings: +2.7 for ~3 s), a charge on routers (no burst measured: contact.pursuit_why), collision damage (all our models are small), the bonus only against the order's target (the network nearly always strikes its target; contact.unit_incidental cuts the rest).

kills.why: men lost per HP lost: blows that do not kill wound; men share = max(1 - g (1 - hp share), hp share), g = (hits to kill)^-exponent; fitted to men against health in the pairs (at half health: slaves 0.6 of men, spearmen 0.7-0.78; lords kill whole men: 1)

missile.reload_ref_why: reload_s was measured on the archers (passport 10 s) and the skavenslave slingers (9 s); another unit of the category gets reload_s x its passport reload / this (the Night Runners' sling, passport 8 s: 10.2 s). Not measured for them.
missile.musket_why: ESTIMATE, not measured (02.10.2026): Free Company Militia pistols (category musket, trajectory low = direct fire, range 90 m, passport reload 9 s -> 10.8 s by reload_scale_other, aim_s_other). The projectile's calibration area is 2.0 m at 65 m against the arrow's 3.7 m at 95 m: at the edge of range the pistol spreads 2.0 x 90 / 65 = 2.8 m, the arrow 3.7 x 125 / 95 = 4.9 m; a flat shot also carries on through the ranks (penetration low: up to 2 men). 0.5 x the distance factor at 60-90 m (1.12-1.29) gives 0.56-0.65 hits per shot, between the arrow's 0.42 and 1 / spread scaling (0.74). To measure: docs/en/training/units.md, recordings wanted.
missile.single_in_melee_why: single_entity_in_melee: the share of the hits aimed at a lone man (a lord) that he takes while he is in melee (1: whole; out of melee single_entity_factor 0.43). Of the hits aimed at a unit in melee the shooter's friendly_fire share still lands on its own units in contact. Measured (build/batch3/lord_shot.py; the replay of 22 gate battles x 6 copies, both sides on their recorded orders): our lord in melee loses 0.62 / 0.82 % of his health a second with 1 / 2+ enemy missile units firing at him in the game, the simulator with 0.43: 0.42 / 0.50, with 1: 0.59 / 0.87 (not shot: game 0.47, simulator 0.28-0.30, another gap). The 0.43 was measured on lords out of melee for the whole flight (~33k shots), so it stays there.
missile.physical_resist_why: physical_resist: a projectile's damage is cut by the target's missile and physical resistance together, at most 90 % (CA, Feature Focus 'Damage': physical resistance works against all non-magical damage; the resistances add, capped at 90 %). Before only missile resistance counted. It touches the Night Runners (physical 20 %) and Strength of the Penitent (+15 % physical) today. damage_mod_all (a ward save, 0 for every unit) is read into the physical resistance (params.py), so it counts once for melee and missiles. Alone it leaves the mechanics check at 51 of 54 (build/prespec/mech_resist.json).
missile.stand_fire_why: stand_fire_arc_deg 45: standing, a unit shoots only at targets within this angle of its facing; one beyond it is turned to first (turn.formation_deg_s) and aimed at (aim_s) only once within it; without an ordered target the nearest within the arc is taken, else the unit turns to the nearest beyond it. Measured 04.10.2026 (build/p3, 210 arena runs): the volleys of standing missile units out of melee (84.5k, ammo a man dropping >= 0.03 in a second) are within 15 deg of the direction to the engine's target (else the nearest enemy) 70.6 %, 15-30 deg 23.7 %, 30-45 deg 4.8 %, 45-60 deg 0.7 %, beyond 60 deg 0.3 % (p95 31, p99 45; each unit type p99 31-47, militia 121 from its moving fire). A new engine target while standing, no volley in the 3 s before: the first volley 2 s later (median) at 0-40 deg off, 3 s at 60-180 deg (the turn about 1 s). 180: off.
missile.volley_why: volley_load 1: the unit shoots once all its men are loaded, so whole-unit volleys one reload apart (the archer range: ~80 of 90 arrows within 1 s of the first, then ~10 s nothing; the shooting arenas: volleys one reload apart). 0 was every loaded man at once: a volley, then at once a steady trickle. Measured 04.10.2026 (sim task 2, build/p2/halt.py, reload.py): shooters that halt in battle and stand 12 s or more out of melee with an enemy in range shoot in those 12 s 0.55 projectiles a man (the network's) / 0.72-0.76 (the game AI's), the first shot 4-6 s after the halt (1 s samples; the range gives 2-3 s on the same count), units never shot before 0.82-0.94; the simulator 1.5-1.7 (the volley, then the trickle at once), with 1: 1.0. The men keep reloading on the move: units that shot less than 4 s before moving off shoot after the halt as much as those loaded long before. aim_reset_on_order 1: a new order (another kind or another attack target) makes a shooter aim again (aim_s): in the game a unit that shot in the 3 s before, standing with an enemy in range, given an attack order shoots in 0.35 / 0.26 of its next 10 s (arrows / slings) against 0.47 / 0.42 given no order in 10 s, its first shot 2 / 5 s later against at once; given hold 0.21 / 0.19, 5-7 s (all network runs from 02.10.2026, 23k unit-seconds); the network's halts had a new order between the halt and the first shot 0.92-0.97 of the time. move_fire_arc_deg 90: firing whilst moving (Free Company Militia) only at targets within this angle of the facing (the way it walks): our militia moving 0.5 m/s or more, in range, out of melee shoots 0.52 of its full rate toward the nearest enemy (within 60 deg), 0.31 across, 0.16 away (1.4k s); the simulator 0.57 / 0.75 / 0.83, at 90 deg 0.50 / 0.54 / 0.13. The game AI's militia does not shoot on the move at all (0.00-0.02 of its 1.4k moving seconds in range): its control, not the attribute.
missile.why: measured (measurements.md, shooting at a unit that stands): reload in practice 11.0 s arrows (passport 10) and 11.5 s sling (passport 9); hit rate at the edge of range 0.42 and 0.47; first shot 3.3 and 4.3 s after halting. Other projectiles: the mean, reload x1.2 of the passport. distance_factor: HP per arrow against the distance, relative to 105-130 m, from the range test (28.09.2026, standing spearmen: c = 13.4 at 70 m, 11.6 at 90 m, 9.5-10.4 at 105-120 m), held below 70 m; the arena's 34 m (~25 HP) and 52 m (~18 HP) are left out: they exceed or reach the arrow's whole damage (19), so melee losses are mixed in. single_entity_factor: HP a lord loses per projectile aimed at him while he is out of melee for the whole flight (the shot's second and the 2 s after), against the unit rule with his armour, shield (by the shooter's side), resistance and distance factor: 0.43 over ~33k shots of the 18 mirror and 10 Empire-Skaven battles (General by arrows ~0.5, by sling ~0.37, Warlord by arrows ~0.32; per battle median 0.43). An earlier count gave 0.9: its 2-second loss windows overlapped and counted each loss twice. friendly_fire: of the hits aimed at a unit in melee, the share that lands on the shooter's own units in contact with it. Measured in the recordings: in the seconds a missile unit shoots an enemy that fights its own units (and nobody shoots those units), their HP lost beyond the melee rule (and beyond the 1.15x / 1.5x they lose when their own side does not shoot), against those shots' hits by the unit rule: arrows 0.26 (18 mirror battles, 1.5k seconds), sling 0.56 (10 Empire-Skaven battles, 1.3k seconds); other projectiles: the mean; a lord among those units takes his share x single_entity_factor (a lone target; 01.10.2026, otherwise a lord in melee with shot enemies took the whole friendly fire). spill: of the hits aimed at a unit, the share that lands on each other unit of the target's side out of melee, by the distance between their centres: in the recordings a unit nobody shoots at, out of melee, with an enemy-shot neighbour within 30 m loses 0.115 of the hits that neighbour takes by the unit rule (2.1k seconds), 0.034 at 30-60 m (6.3k), 0.015 at 60-90 m (7.2k), 0.005 beyond (units with no shot neighbour lose 0.7 HP/s); spill_melee: the same for the target's own units that are in melee too, when the target is in melee (01.10.2026, build/nn-sim/flank/spill_melee.py: HP a unit in melee, not shot at itself and whose own side does not shoot its opponents, loses regressed on its melee rule and on the hits aimed at other units of its side in melee, by centre distance: 0.19 within 15 m, 0.047 at 15-30 m, 0.035 at 30-60 m (the 27 net runs and the 28 game-AI battles, 74k seconds, 15k with a shot neighbour; the 28 battles alone 0.23 / 0.09 / 0.16, the net runs 0.19 / 0.05 / 0.035, the far bin taken from the net runs). Before it, only units out of melee took spill, so units fighting around a lord the enemy shoots at (run 20261001-074420) lost nothing to those shots; it is why an infantry unit in a whole battle loses ~1.3x per shot aimed at it what the lone target of the shooting arena does. Without it a unit in melee loses 3.2x the melee rule (Skaven infantry) and 2.2x (Empire infantry, mirror) while its own missile units shoot at the enemy it fights, 1.5x and 1.15x otherwise

morale.lord_why: A lord's own morale. lord_own_aura false: the lord's aura (+4) reaches his army's other units, not himself. Measured (build/lordmorale/aura.py, all recorded runs): a lord at full health, calm, with a friend within 120 m stands at MoralePercent 1.129 (Empire General, 106 lord-battles: without his own aura (70 + 4 Hold the Line + 5) / 70 = 1.129, with it 1.186) and 1.083 (Skaven Warlord, 54: 65 / 60 = 1.083 against 1.150). single_combat 'losing': a single entity in melee always gets the database's losing_combat (-3), whatever the HP balance; missing: by the HP ratio like a formation. The game lords' morale in melee, regressed on the other terms (build/lordmorale/reg.py, combat.py), shows -3.8 points in melee (95 % CI -4.7 ... -3.0), flat in the HP balance (absolute or as shares); the ratio rule gave a lord +4 / +5 (winning) through most of his melee. The milder 'no winning bonus' (combat points capped at 0) gives 0 while even or winning: the measured -3.8 favours -3. With missile.single_entity_in_melee and fatigue.lord_why (batch 3), the replay of 22 gate battles x 6 copies (both sides on their recorded orders, build/batch3/lord_fate.py): our lord routed at least once 0.30 -> 0.44 (game 1.00), dead at the game's end 0.02 -> 0.06 (game 0.14), health left 0.35 -> 0.30 (game 0.11).
morale.windows_why: casualties_window sliding: recent casualties = HP lost in exactly the last casualties_s (4) s, extended casualties = in the last extended_s (60) s (the database's descriptions; its points: recent 6 / 10 / 15 / 33 / 50 % -> -6 ... -80, extended 10 / 15 / 33 / 50 / 80 % -> -4 ... -60); decay: decaying sums with those time constants. under_fire_s: 'under fire' (-5, ume_concerned_attacked_by_projectile) holds this long after the last projectile hit. Measured on the unit read-out probes of 27.09.2026 (build/unit-readout/runs, 1 s samples): the game's IsUnderMissileAttack is on through a barrage and goes off exactly 15 s after the last HP loss in 9 of 9 barrages, and morale starts to rise in that same second; PercentHpLostRecently after a volley holds one value 3 samples, then drops to 0 (a flat window of about 4 s, as the database says). Together (build/prespec/batch2.md section 2.3; the mechanics check's shooting targets, game 39 / 71 s waver / rout after the first shot for the archers' target, 154 / 177 for the slingers'): before (2 s, one decaying 30 s window) 35 / 68 and 154 / 184, 51 of 54; 15 s alone 25 / 68 (the archers' target wavers too early, 50 of 54); 15 s + decaying 4 s and 60 s 66 / 78 (50); 15 s + sliding 4 s and 60 s 46 / 68 and 165 / 184 (51); 15 s + sliding 4 s alone 68 / 90 (49). The single decaying 30 s window was fitted while 'under fire' lasted 2 s and stood in for it.
morale.expendable_why: expendable_scares_expendable: a routing expendable unit (attribute expendable: Skavenslaves) scares other expendable units within 100 m (-3 each, routing_friends) and no other unit; false: it scares nobody (the old rule). The database's attribute text: its rout scares only expendable units. Measured (build/prespec/batch2.md item 5, all fair recordings with morale): an expendable unit with one expendable friend newly routing within 100 m drops 3.0 points in 4 s (median, 350 cases); a normal unit at an expendable friend's rout 0.0 (178); the background 0.0.
morale.strong_enemy_why: strong_enemy_points: points while a standing enemy worth more (cost x health) is within 70 m; the database's enemy_morale_penalty_value_min is -3. Measured 0 (build/prespec/batch2.md item 8): 3,244 times one standing enemy came within 70 m of a unit out of melee (no threat flags, no losses, no routing units near), its points 4 s later changed by 0.0 (median) whatever the worth ratio (below 1: 1,560; 1-2: 1,098; 2-4: 518; 4 and more: 68), mean +0.3 ... +0.5 in every bin. So the -3 does not show in the game out of melee (the Sol audit's scale to -24 neither). KEPT at the database's -3 (0 is the measured value, left off): with 0 the mechanics check falls 51 -> 50 of 54 with the rest of batch 2 on: in pair_spear_v_clanrat the spearmen, without the -3 for the clanrats near them through the whole fight, waver at 287 s against the game's 251 (253 with it) and rout at 302 against 275 (291), and the clanrats then waver at 295 s, which they never do in the game. So in melee the -3 (or something it stands in for) shows; the record count was out of melee only.

collapse.why: CCO morale fields in 69 of 175 completed fair battles (build/collapse): 65 sides show Army losses. BalanceOfPowerPercent is reconstructed by strategic_value with routers weighted 0.5 (mean absolute bar error 0.00041 versus 0.0121 at full weight); shattered units contribute zero. The database's 2.6 enemy/own and 0.22 own/start thresholds on that strength time 64/65 onsets within 5 s (median 0 s, mean absolute error 0.57 s). Three additional triggers occur only in final frames after the last standing unit routes, not before defeat. Value follows HP, not men. Starting lord values are 950/900 versus multiplayer cost 600/525: approximate with lord_value_scale 1.65. Missile value is HP times a normalised sigmoid of whole-unit ammunition remaining: slope 14, midpoint 0.25, empty fractions 0.309/0.312/0.323 for archers/slingers/night runners and 0.570 for direct-fire Free Company. Generic floors 0.32/0.57 plus the lord scale approximate the recorded pools (bar error 0.0051, 58/65 onsets within 5 s, no missed onsets, median 0 s); other missile types are not fitted. Army losses propagate globally: 271/275 units standing just before onset show the effect, median delay 0 s; median routing friends within 100 m is 0. All 274 army-loss shatters before a third rout cross the database's broken lower edge (-50 points). Routers keep losing morale under army destruction even away from enemies and cannot rally out of it. No lord-fall points tie in (a routed lord costs his aura only, lord_fall.why): 33/65 onsets have a standing lord; 42/65 have no friend newly routing in the previous 3 s. Full-strength routers were rejected: three-gate replay trade -0.090/-0.081/-0.244 versus baseline -0.090/-0.080/-0.252; the apparent 59/65 onset match mainly followed shattering instead of predicting it. Shattering below -50 is limited to army destruction. At game end, scoped replay trade is -0.094/-0.088/-0.246 versus baseline -0.090/-0.080/-0.252 (game -0.306/-0.260/-0.407): mean absolute trade error 0.18356 to 0.18137, but the third gate regresses, so the all-three acceptance criterion is unmet. In the first copies only 3/22 own armies reach the measured conditions by game end; prior combat divergence remains.

morale.rally_why: rally_rule: 'fixed' (ON): a routing unit free of enemies rallies at MoralePercent rally_mp. 'target' (measured, left OFF): it rallies once its morale is above 0 and within rally_gap_mp (x leadership) of its morale target, and only if that target is above rally_target_min_mp (x leadership); rally_cap: no later than at rally_mp. The game (build/batch3/rally_game.py, 3,678 rallies in 235 recordings): MoralePercent at the rally depends on health, 0.08 / 0.24 / 0.47 (median) below 0.2 / 0.2-0.4 / 0.4-0.7 of it, and rises after the rally to 0.22 / 0.42 / 0.64 at 45 s: a rally comes 0.14-0.18 of leadership below the morale the unit then settles at. The casualty table is the database's for rallied and never-routed units alike (calm Empire units, build/batch3/calm_pen.py): no reset at a rally. With 'fixed' the simulator rallies at 0.23 units whose target is far lower (half the AI's rallies under 20 % health): their morale falls (0.23 -> 0.09 in 5 s) and 0.40 rout again when the 10 s post-rally protection ends (game 0.07). Replay of 22 gate battles x 6 copies, the AI's units (build/batch3/rally_metrics.py; counts per unit by build/routgap/analyse.py): re-routed 10 / 20 / 30 / 45 s after a rally game 0.07 / 0.13 / 0.16 / 0.23, fixed 0.40 / 0.43 / 0.46 / 0.51, target (gap 0.17, min 0) 0.06 / 0.14 / 0.20 / 0.29, target with min -0.17 0.29 / 0.34 / 0.39 / 0.47; morale after a rally game 0.17 -> 0.29 at 10 s, fixed 0.23 -> 0.09 at 5 s, target 0.13 -> 0.27. Rallies / re-routs / routs per AI unit: game 0.42 / 0.24 / 0.61, fixed 0.46 / 0.35 / 0.74, target 0.27 / 0.16 / 0.55, min -0.17 0.35 / 0.24 / 0.63 (gaps 0.10 / 0.25, the cap: within 0.01); our units' routs game 1.57, fixed 1.09, target 0.93. Mechanics 51 / 54 with each. Gap card of gate 20261005-161910 (8 copies, items 1-4 of batch 3 on): routs per unit own / enemy game 1.52 / 0.58, fixed 1.04 / 1.08, target 0.85 / 0.84; trade game -0.385, fixed +0.037, target +0.022 (min -0.17: 1.02 / 0.92, +0.009). The whole check (tools.nn.sim.check): routs / rallies a battle game 22.5 / 13.0, fixed 18.1 / 10.9, target 13.0 / 5.9; same winner game-AI 22 / 26 -> 21, network 122 / 163 -> 123. Left OFF: no variant meets both the counts and the timing (the game also rallies units with nothing left, and they rout again gradually, not at 10 s; that rule is not found).

lord_fall.why: A lord's fall: his aura goes (battle.py: the aura counts standing lords only) and, on top, his army's other units get points by HOW he fell. KILLED (health 0): the database's ume_concerned_general_died_recently -16 for recent_s, then ume_concerned_general_dead -10 to the end (killed: true). Routed OFF THE MAP (gone with men left): ume_concerned_general_fled_recently -16 for fled_s, then nothing (fled: true). ROUTED or shattered, still on the field: `routed` points (0: the aura alone). rout_death_s: a faction whose routed lord crumbles to death counts him killed that long into his rout. Measured 05.10.2026 (tools/nn/lord_fall.py, 15 in-game battles, build/lord-fall/analysis.json; build/lorddeath/timeline.py): the lord killed at a fixed moment, 20 s into melee (Empire, Skaven, Vampire Counts, 2 battles each): the two idle units out of his aura and 115+ m from any enemy (12 unit-deaths) show 'general died recently' and drop -3 / -7 / -13.5 / -16 points 1 / 2 / 5 / 10 s after, hold -16, the effect turns into 'general dead' at 45.5-46 s and the units stand at -10 from ~50 s to the recording's end (60 s); identical in all three factions. The ramp is the morale update itself (max(1, 15 % of the gap) a 0.5 s tick: a step of -16 gives -4.4 / -7.6 / -12.9 / -15.4), so the points are a step. The two fighting units within his aura: -6 / -10 / -17.5 / -21...-25 at 1 / 2 / 5 / 10 s (aura and melee on top). The lord routed by script (morale_behavior_rout; Empire, Skaven, 2 battles each): the idle units 0 at every moment, the fighting ones about the aura (-0.5...-6.8 at 10 s net of the control); general_fled_recently does not show while the lord is on the field. Leaving the map (build/prespec/specs.md section 1, recorded battles with morale texts from 02.10.2026): a shattered lord who routs off the map edge (4 cases, 10-17 % health) gives his army 'general fled recently': the standing units -14...-17 points within 10 s (3 battles, 18 units), the effect lasts ~120 s (747 -> 867 s, 782 -> 901 s; the other two recordings ended sooner) and no 'general dead' follows: fled_s 120 (2 timed cases, medium confidence). A lord killed while routing (4 cases) gives the same 'died recently' -> 'dead' after 45 s. Vampire Counts' routed lord shatters and crumbles (health -12 % a second), dies at 8-8.5 s, and his army gets 'general died recently' from 8.5 s, 'general dead' from 53.5 s: rout_death_s 8 (the simulator has no Vampire Counts units: config only). The same battles in the simulator (build/lorddeath/sim_fall.py: the recorded places, Empire and Skaven, the fight pairs attacking, the enemy held fearless): idle units -4.4 / -7.6 / -14 / -16 / -16 / -16 / -10 at 1 / 2 / 5 / 10 / 20 / 40 / 60 s after the death (game -3 / -7 / -13.5 / -16 / -16 / -16 / -10; 0 throughout before this rule), fighting units net of the control -5.5 / -9.6 / -16 / -20 / -20 / -20 / -14 (game, Empire and Skaven -6.4 / -9.3 / -16.5 / -16 / -16.9 / -19.1 / -13.5; before -2 / -4 / -4 / -4 / -4 / -4 / -4); the rout: idle 0, fighting -2 / -4 / -7 / -7 / -4 / -4 / -4 (game -2.6 / -3.6 / -7 / -3.3 / -0.3 / -2.6 / -0.5), unchanged. Natural falls (02.10.2026, build/simacc/lordfall2.py): in all 75 recorded lord falls of the fair battles the lord shattered with 2-50 % of his health left (none was killed), and the standing units of his army (167 unit-falls, 35 falls) changed by 0 points in the 10 s before, -1 at the fall, -3.2 / -4.3 / -4.7 / -4.8 (mean; median -3) 2 / 4 / 6 / 10 s after, -7 at 20 s - about the aura; the database's -16 / -10 on every fall gave -9 / -14 / -17 / -18 and routed 39 % of the army within 10 s (the game 21 %). So from task 20 to 05.10.2026 every fall was 0 / 0 (right for routs, wrong for deaths). The armies' collapse at the end of the game's battles is a rule not tied to the lord (collapse.why).

morale.why: Task 20 (02.10.2026, build/simacc/kb_eval.py, kb_events.py, collapse.py; docs/en/game/mechanics/README.md conflicts): casualties_s / extended_s / casualties_window / under_fire_s: windows_why (the database's 4 s and 60 s as sliding windows, with 'under fire' 15 s). Before, one decaying 30 s window (extended_s 0) kept 51 of 54 while 'under fire' lasted 2 s: taken alone, the database's windows (decaying 4 s + 60 s) made the archers' target waver 90 % late (73 s against 39 s) and the slingers' never; 10 s: +54 %; 30 s + 60 s: the pairs wavered too early (47 of 54). attacked_event: the database's was_attacked_in_flank / _rear -6 / -14 for the 0.5 s tick a unit is first struck from a worse side (battle.py), instead of the regressed -1 / -2 while struck: in the 91 recordings a unit first struck in the flank drops 1.5 points more over 1-2 s than one first struck in front (309 / 1457 contacts), in the rear 1.9 more (202) - one tick of -6 / -14 (1 and 2.1 points); a new attacker on a unit already fighting: 0.4-0.9 more. aura_fade: the lord's +4 fades from 70 m to 0 at 105 m (inspiration_radius_max_effect_range_modifier 1.5). collapse: army destruction uses the recorded strategic-value approximation and the database's 2.6 / 0.22 thresholds; see collapse.why.  Not modelled, checked: charge morale (the database's charge_bonus +15 / charge_timeout 60): a unit that runs into contact (3343 contacts) loses as much morale over the next 1-4 s as one met standing (1500), no +15 shows. lord_fall: see lord_fall.why. faction_bonus: before contact Skaven units stand 6 points higher than the Empire's in the same place (slaves, clanrats, slingers; pairs, shooting, whole battles): that is Strength in Numbers' +6 (stat_morale, while health is above 50 % of the start), an innate effect since 02.10.2026 (config/nn/effects.json), so the bonus is 0 for every faction now (the Warlord, who lacks Strength in Numbers, lost the +6; it was never measured on him). recent_s: the time constant of the melee balance (HP dealt / taken, winning or losing the melee; reward.py reads the same); recent_of_current: whether the recent casualties' share is of the health left (false: of the start). combat_ratio: melee HP dealt / taken for winning slightly, winning, significantly (the database gives only the points). rally_mp: a routing unit rallies at MoralePercent ~0.23 (morale.md, median 0.22 at 365 rallies). rally_free_m: no standing enemy that near (at 365 rallies of the mirror and Empire-Skaven battles the nearest standing enemy was 91 m or more in 90 %). rally_rate: points a second a routing unit regains while free, calibrated to the rallies of the whole battles (median 44 s). rout_floor_mp: where morale stands at most when the rout begins (recorded MoralePercent at the rout: median -0.03, 10 % below -0.17). rout_speed: a routing unit runs at this share of its run speed WITH its fatigue (battle.py: u['run'] already carries the fatigue state's scalar_speed and the innate effects). 0.985 (build/prespec/batch2.md item 2): the routing speed over the run divided by the database's fatigue multiplier is 0.989 / 1.000 / 0.994 / 0.997 / 0.992 / 0.990 for Empire units fresh ... exhausted (16 / 13 / 14 / 15 / 28 / 49k s), 0.977 / 0.976 for Skaven (run x Scurry Away! x Strength in Numbers x fatigue, 120 / 12k s). The older 0.86 below was the median of routers that were nearly all tired: the fatigue counted twice. Measured 02.10.2026 (all fair recordings with unit keys, game-AI and network runs; speed over 1 s steps at least 3 s into a rout, moving): Empire units 0.865 of the run (median, 115k s), Skaven 0.945 below half health (186k s) and 0.866 above it (14k s): Scurry Away! (x1.1 while wavering or routing) and Strength in Numbers (x0.9 while health is above half) give 0.86 x 1.1 = 0.95 and 0.86 x 0.99 = 0.85. Running in order, not wavering, above half health: Empire 0.97, Skaven 0.88 (x0.91 = Strength in Numbers' x0.9). attacked_flank / attacked_rear: points while an enemy strikes from the flank / rear, instead of the database's was_attacked_in_flank -6 / _rear -14: regressing morale points - leadership of infantry in melee in the 28 whole battles (30k seconds; on health lost, flank, rear, contacts, the lf/rf/bf flags, under fire) gives -1.0 / -1.8, while the same regression on the simulator with the database's points gives -1 / -14.5. The same regression gives -3.9 / -8.1 for one / several of lf, rf, bf: the database's ume_concerned_flanks_exposed_single / _multiple -3 / -6, used as they are

fatigue.lord_why: A single entity's (a lord's) melee: calibration.single_combat 15 a tick (missing: the database's +19) and the charge cost (+34) only in the first 2 s (calibration.charge_s, now every unit's) (missing: while his charge lasts, 13 s, so a lord that charged in paid 4,400 points, two thirds of 'winded', in his first 13 s). Measured: the game's lords first turn tired after 62 / 60 s of melee (our / the AI's, median, the 22 gate battles), the simulator before after 37 / 47 s, with the 2 s charge 46 / 58 s, with it and 12 a tick 67 / 86 s, with 15 55 / 72 s (build/lordmorale/lordfat.py). The replay of the 204 recordings (build/batch3/run.py fat): lords exhausted our / AI game 22.0 / 22.9 % of their seconds, tired or worse 46.0 / 48.4 %; before 24.1 / 41.8 % and 49.7 / 64.6 %; the 2 s charge alone 17.3 / 34.1 % and 49.8 / 64.8 %; with 12 a tick 8.5 / 15.9 % and 38.5 / 54.0 %; with 15 13.6 / 25.3 % and 45.7 / 59.5 % (taken: the smallest sum of errors). The AI's lord stays more tired than in the game whatever the rate (he fights more in the replay); one rate cannot fit both. All units' exhausted share in that replay: own / enemy 16.4 / 28.2 % -> 14.9 / 25.8 % (game 17.3 / 28.6 %); units without lords 15.6 / 26.8 -> 15.1 / 25.9 % (game 16.9 / 29.2 %; that shift comes from the lord's morale and missile rules, not this one).

calibration.why: ON (production). Rule: 10 ticks/s, each unit in one activity. Melee costs points only under an attack order: +15 a tick for a single entity (single_combat: fatigue.lord_why), 13.7 for a formation; in melee without one the unit moves (by its run flag) or rests -18. Charging +34 only with the order and only in the first charge_s 2 s after a charge's first blow, for every unit (build/charge/spec.md C6: after a contact at a run the game's units leave 'fresh' after 17 s, median of 456; +34 for the charge's whole 13 s gave ~8 s; before 06.10.2026 the 2 s held only for a lone man, single_charge_s). A move costs by its order's run flag whatever the speed: run +4, walk -1 (database). A routing unit tires at the running +4. Shooting 7.5. Standing without unfinished movement, attack or aiming: idle -18 when no standing enemy is within 80 m, else ready -7. Dead and departed slots frozen. Evidence: per-unit activity classes of the 204 fair recordings fitted to the game's recorded states (build/fat/opus classes.py): formation melee with a target 13.86, shooting 7.15 a tick (bootstrap 13.6-14.5 / 6.5-7.6); a lord fighting fits +19; units in melee without a target recover; routing 5.1 a tick (running +4). Clean walk-only spans of game-AI units under a walk order (2925 s): 0 up / 6 down state crossings, so walking recovers at the database -1; the earlier fitted +3.4 came from run-order moves at low speed (build/fat/opus/gate_check/walk_noflag.py). Standing units of the network's recordings recover at 0.48 / 0.62 / 0.79 / 1.00 of idle -18 with the nearest standing enemy within 40 / 40-80 / 80-150 / 150-300 m, the simulator at 0.9-1.1 (build/agent_fatv3/near2.py). Replay of the 204 recordings: exhausted own / enemy 17.06 / 29.05% versus game 17.34 / 28.61%; late own 29.07 versus 30.29%; the warlord pair's spearmen exhaust at 231/232/232 s versus game 226/229/230 s. Closed loop on the starts of gate 20261005-161910 (network s6_fatigue/m20 against ai_like, 4 copies): own exhausted at 240-360 / 360+ s 37.0 / 59.8% versus game 51.8 / 79.8% (before this rule 43.8 / 56.8%), fresh 3.6 / 7.4% versus game 0.1 / 0.0% (before 1.9 / 11.3%): the rest of the gap is time spent standing (own still seconds after 180 s: 23% versus 13% in the network's game recordings), recovering at the game's rate. Frozen check: mechanics 51/54, game-AI 23/26, network 96/132. Data: build/fat/opus, build/agent_fatv3.

fatigue.why: per_second 5 with the database rates (melee +19 for every engaged unit, ready -7 as rest, inactive slots included) is the legacy model, used only when calibration.on is false. DB thresholds and unit_fatigue_effects_tables multipliers apply in both.

threat.why: Enabled geometry: a non-routing enemy within 45 m, front/rear boundaries 60/150 degrees, facing the unit within 60 degrees, evaluated after movement and turning. Native lf/rf/bf remain is_left_flank_threatened/is_right_flank_threatened/is_rear_flank_threatened, unchanged through companion. Adoption prioritizes direct input correction: threat-only closed-loop rear flags own/enemy 0.049/0.047 versus game 0.072/0.044 and legacy 0.319/0.306. Not fully calibrated: side/out-of-melee residuals exceed battle-bootstrap noise; mechanics 51/54, game-AI 20/26, network 100/132 versus legacy 51/54, 23/26, 99/132. Both ON gives 49/54, 22/26, 100/132 and exposes an invalid fatigue-participation assumption, so fatigue remains OFF. Shared observation and exposed-flank morale flags; actual attacked-from-flank/rear events still use incoming contact sectors. No thinning or game-side remapping. Evidence: build/agent-fatigue2 and build/agent-fatigue3.

effects.off_why: off: effects the catalogue could model but the simulator leaves out (a calibration switch; each entry needs its reason here). Single Entity (the lords: speed x0.9, melee damage and AP x0.8 while health is below 25 %, by our reading of its recharge context health_below_25%; the knowledge base: WH3 single entities have a 'wounded' state at low health, thresholds not found): in the recordings (02.10.2026, all fair runs with unit keys) lords running out of melee move at 0.84-0.85 of their run in every health band (0.35-0.5, 0.25-0.35, 0.15-0.25, below 0.15; 4.9k-8.6k s each): no x0.9 below 25 %. On, it flipped two mirror battles whose replays split (5 of 8 and 4 of 8 before) and kept one more at 32 replays (same winner 20 of 26 against 21). Left out until a lord below 25 % health is recorded with the bridge's ActiveEffectList (units.md, recordings wanted). The network still sees it (owned; on by its condition).
effects.why: Innate effects (tools/nn/sim/effects.py, config/nn/effects.json from the game's database by python -m tools.nn.effects): every attribute and passive or game-fired ability of a unit, one mechanism; the catalogue's `modelled` effects are laid on. No numbers here: the stats, conditions and timers are the database's. Strength in Numbers and Scurry Away! were left out on 02.10.2026 when they alone made the pairs worse (50 of 54): then Strength in Numbers' +6 came on top of the fitted Skaven morale.faction_bonus +6 (the same thing counted twice) and Scurry Away! on top of one rout_speed fitted to both factions. With faction_bonus 0 and rout_speed refitted to the Empire (morale why) they are modelled as the database says.

abilities.why: Lord abilities (tools/nn/sim/abilities.py). The numbers (active and recharge time, range, targets, effects) are the ability passports, config/nn/abilities.json (py -3.14 -m tools.nn.abilities, the game's database); what each unit owns: units.json abilities (the slots: tools/nn/sim/abilities.py slot_keys). model: the cast abilities whose effects the simulator lays on (the lords' actives). Effects modelled: scalar_speed (walk, run, and the charge speed unless scalar_charge_speed is given), scalar_charge_speed, melee attack and defence (add), melee damage base and AP (mult), charge bonus (mult), stat_morale (add, morale points). Verminous Valour's 25 m, 1 s blast (battle_vortexs) has damage 0 and AP 0 (hand decode): not modelled. triggers: when the game's AI fires an active: melee = its lord is in melee, near = a standing enemy within near_m of him, waver = a friend within range_m wavers or routs, never = not at all; friends_min: only with at least this many standing friends within the ability's range_m; default_trigger for an active not listed. Each fires again as soon as it is ready while its rule holds. Measured 06.10.2026 (build/lordduel/abilities: the active effects, nn_effects, of the game's AI lords in 139 gate battles, 85 Generals and 54 Warlords, 926 uses; a rule fits a use when it first turns true within 2 s of it; false = ready lord-seconds with the rule true and no use): Foe-Seeker and Verminous Valour in melee (fit 218 of 318 / 182 of 245, false 19 / 13 s; the old 'enemy within 60 m' 160 / 119, false 2050 / 1537 s): ~30 % at contact, ~40 % the moment they are ready again in melee, the rest a few seconds before contact (median 12 m); Stand Your Ground in melee with >= 1 friend within 35 m (136 of 206, false 16 s; melee alone 116, false 3014 s); Rally in melee with >= 2 friends within 35 m (69 of 157, false 62 s - the loosest: a wavering friend within 35 m at only 27 % of its uses; the old 'waver' 24 of 157, false 1830 s); Deadly Onslaught never (0 uses; 'in melee' held 10,588 ready seconds in 53 of 54 battles). The lone lord duels (build/lord-ai, 12 battles under the AI): only Foe-Seeker / Verminous Valour, 0-1 s after contact, again 85-86 / 77-78 s later (active + recharge); never Stand Your Ground, Rally or Deadly Onslaught. The lord's health does not change any of them. Before (an assumption): Deadly Onslaught and Stand Your Ground in melee, the speed abilities with an enemy within 60 m, Rally on a wavering friend. The network fires its lord's self-cast actives by order (Orders.ability). Passive and game-fired abilities (Hold the Line, Frenzy, Strength of the Penitent, Strength in Numbers, Scurry Away!, Single Entity) are innate effects since 02.10.2026 (`effects`): `model` lists only what this section lays on itself. Ready again recharge_s after the active time ends; ready at the start (no initial recharge found).
